info.name: agentic-rag-platform
info.description:
Example requests for the local [agentic-rag-platform](https://github.com/saequus/agentic-rag-platform) API.

Start the API from the repo root:

    uv run fastapi dev src/agentic_rag_platform/main.py --port 8000

Interactive OpenAPI docs: [http://localhost:8000/docs](http://localhost:8000/docs)

Machine-readable OpenAPI schema: [http://localhost:8000/openapi.json](http://localhost:8000/openapi.json)

Select the **local** environment (`baseUrl=http://localhost:8000`, `tenantId=default`). Collection variables have the same defaults and also define `corpusPath` and `samplePdfPath`.

Endpoints covered: `GET /health`, `POST /chat`, `POST /chat/stream`, `POST /chat/resume`, `GET /chat/{thread_id}` (Day 4 agent), `POST /chat/loop` (Day 1 loop), `POST /ingest`, `POST /search`.

Notes:

- There is no request-body field to override the LLM provider. The running process uses `LLM_PROVIDER` from `.env` (`xai` by default, or `openai` / `anthropic`). Restart the API after changing it.
- Search uses `k` (1–100), not `top_k`. Tenant scoping is `tenant_id`.
- `POST /ingest` resolves `source_path` on the API host. The "Ingest corpus" request embeds every PDF under `data/raw` and can take several minutes — prefer the single-file request unless you intend a full ingest.
- Example responses are illustrative (from unit tests and the README), not live captures.

item.name: Agent (Day 4, LangGraph)
item.description: LangGraph agent with Postgres checkpoints (`thread_id` memory), SSE streaming and a human-approval interrupt before the `save_note` write tool. See README 'Day 4: LangGraph agent'.

request.description: Runs the LangGraph agent: route -> retrieve -> grade_docs -> (rewrite_query) -> generate -> check_grounded. `thread_id` is the conversation memory key; omit it to get a new one in the response. `strategy` / `backend` are optional (default RETRIEVAL_STRATEGY / RETRIEVAL_BACKEND).

body.raw:
{
  "message": "Jakie jest oprocentowanie obligacji EDO1136 w pierwszym okresie odsetkowym?",
  "thread_id": "{{threadId}}",
  "tenant_id": "{{tenantId}}",
  "strategy": "hybrid_rerank",
  "backend": "pgvector"
}

request.description: Uses thread memory from the checkpointer: the previous turn is in the prompt, so the follow-up resolves to EDO1136.

Server-Sent Events: `start`, `node` (one per graph node, metadata only), `token` (text deltas), `interrupt`, `done` (final response; render this one: it is the fallback if grounding failed). In Postman the events appear in the response pane as they arrive.

The router picks the `save_note` write tool. The `approval` node calls `interrupt()`: the response has `status: interrupted` and `pending_approval` (tool + arguments). Nothing is written until /chat/resume approves.
Resumes the interrupted thread with `Command(resume={approved: true})`. The approval node re-runs from the top, `interrupt()` returns the decision, and the note is saved. A second resume returns 409.
Rejecting path. Run 'Write action -> approval interrupt' again first (a thread can only be resumed while an approval is pending; otherwise 409).
Returns the thread's messages (short-term memory) and any pending approval. Another tenant gets 404.

item.name: Ingest
item.description: Lab endpoint: `source_path` is a local file or directory on the API host, not an upload. The full-corpus request is slow; use the single-file request for a quick check.

exec: pm.test('JSON shape: tenant_id and documents[]', function () {

request.description: Ingest every PDF under `source_path` (resolved on the machine running the API). Default `corpusPath` is `data/raw`, relative to the repo root — the usual cwd when you run `uv run fastapi dev src/agentic_rag_platform/main.py --port 8000`. This re-embeds the full Day 2 corpus and can take several minutes; it also loads the local embedding model on first use. Prefer the single-file request unless you intend a full ingest.

body.raw:
{
  "query": "Jakie jest oprocentowanie obligacji EDO1136 w pierwszym okresie odsetkowym?",
  "tenant_id": "{{tenantId}}",
  "k": 5,
  "strategy": "hybrid_rerank",
  "backend": "qdrant"
}

request.description: Day 3. Dense + BM25 sparse prefetch fused with RRF in Qdrant, then a cross-encoder rescoring the top 50. Needs Qdrant (`make qdrant-up && make qdrant-sync`, or embedded mode). `timings_ms` shows embed / search / rerank time.

body.raw:
{
  "query": "What did the Governing Council decide at its meeting on 10 September 2026?",
  "tenant_id": "{{tenantId}}",
  "k": 5,
  "strategy": "hybrid",
  "backend": "pgvector"
}

request.description: Day 3. pgvector HNSW top 50 + Postgres full-text (tsvector, 'simple' config) top 50, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion in one SQL query. Needs `make db-init` (migration 002).
Day 3. Lexical search only: shows why exact identifiers (bond series, ISINs, dates) need the sparse leg.
